heading: Menu actions
body:
An item with an `action` calls a method of an application service. Such a service is a Rust service in `client/services/` with `#[Lifetime({"value":"application"})]`. It starts with the app and stops when the app quits, so the method also works when no page is open. It lives only inside the app: Tachyon never installs a system service or starts it at login. Application services work in native macOS, Linux and Windows apps. The browser, iOS and Android cannot own one, so the build stops with `TY1406` there. The `action` names the `service` (its type name) and the `method` (a method that takes only `&self`). The return value of the method is ignored. Selecting the item never loads a page, so the page keeps its state: its fields, the text in its inputs and its scroll position.

To change the page, the application service forwards an event. It gets `CurrentPageEvents` by injection and calls `publish_event` with a model from `client/models`. Every live Rust page service with an `OnEvent` listener for that model receives it, as with any other event. A page service that two components share receives it once, and each prototype instance receives it once. `publish_event` answers `false` when the page has no listener. Only Rust page services receive the event directly, because only they can inject an application service. A JavaScript or TypeScript page service can listen to an event that a Rust listener returns. A listener cannot publish to the page again while it receives the event.

The optional `event` names the model that the method forwards. Tachyon uses it to decide when the item is enabled (see the next section). The build checks each action: the service must be a client Rust service with an application lifetime, the method must exist and take only `&self`, and the event must be a Rust model in `client/models`. Otherwise the build stops with `TY1370`.

Menu actions are Rust only. The host calls the generated Rust service module, and only a client Rust service can have the application lifetime. So this section has no JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Go, Ruby, Python, Lua, Swift, Kotlin, Java, C# or F# tab: a service in one of these languages cannot be the `service` of an action (`TY1370`), but it can still run on the page that the action changes. C++ has no tab here, because the build refuses Lifetime "application" in C++ Tac code: a C++ service runs in the page and has no native host (ADR 0099).
